page.layout: One page of running text. Margin notes in the left margin: "De vi- / ta cont." beside the first lines, "1.2.c.18" beside the fourth line, and "Ps.34." beside the line "admodum alibi". The page number and running head are at the top. A catchword "bus" stands at the lower right.

main_text.p: berationem? Scitum est enim quod aliquan-De vi-ta cont. do Profper discipulus Augustini dicebat: Dulcior fit salus cum dolor excruciat, & fa-1.2.c.18nitatis amissae dulcedinem languoris amari-tudo commendat. Itaque cum hic a nostro vate doceamur a Deo nos seruari, meminerimus hanc esse piorum cōditionem vt eorum vita multis afflictionum telis propofita sit: quandoquidē non opus est salute, si nulla urgeat periculi necessitas: neque futurus est seruator, vbi non sint qui feruari debeant. Hoc ergo seruādi vocabulum satis nos admonet quot quantisque malis atque periculis vita nostra sit obnoxia. Quod etiam confirmant ea quæ sequuntur.

Me, inquit, liberationis caticis[?] circundabis, Hic liberandi verbum manifeste significat res aduersas periculorumque grauitate, quē-Ps.34.admodum alibi noster Psaltes: multa, inquit, mala iusto accidunt, sed illum Dominus ex-omnibus liberat. Nec leuiter praetereundum est circundandi vocabulum, quod arguit nos ab omnibus partibus vrgeri, donec auxilij diuini lux undique circunfusa tenebras afflictionum discutiat. Ac videte, obsecro, quàm egregiè crescat oratio: nec enim tantū Deus est nobis latibulum ac perfugium ad quod recurramus aduersus vim atque impetum hostium, sed nos etiā ab hostibus seruat atque liberat: nec rursus tantùm nos seruat, sed etiam facit, vt de victis prostratrisque hosti-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "caticis" in the italic quotation (the word may be "catenis"; marked [?]). "1.2.c.18" is hard to read; the first character may be "l" or "I". The line break "meminerí / mus" and "vr / geat" show no printed hyphen, so the words are written whole. The long s is set as plain s throughout, including in "seruari", "seruādi" and "seruator", where the letter could also be read as f. "Ps.34." is copied as "Ps." although the letter looks like a long s followed by p. The word "bus" at the foot is a catchword. The left edge of the scan carries show-through from the facing page, which is not transcribed.
